newsitem.title: USA: Capital flows to emerging marts to continue - EBRD.
newsitem.headline: Capital flows to emerging marts to continue - EBRD.

text.p: WASHINGTON, Sept 29 - The surge in private capital flows to emerging markets is not a short-term phenomenon, and multilateral development banks (MDBs) must adapt, the head of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development said.
"Ultimately, MDBs may not be needed," EBRD President Jacques de Larosiere said in a foundation lecture Sunday. "That time has not yet come. They still have important goals."
He argued that the banks should help those countries that have not benefitted from surging private capital flows develop their private sectors.
"There is every indication these flows are not a short-term phenomenon," de Larosiere said. "The oppurtunities in these markets remain great and growing."
He said that investors are not providing funds indiscriminately, but instead are closely monitoring the fundamentals of the countries in which they invest.
"The current flows ... represent more efficient and productive investment than earlier (commercial) bank loans to governments for general financing requirements," he said.
